nodes.summary: Given a type of atoms and a type of agents, the formulas of epistemic logic are built inductively: every atom $p$ is a formula, falsity $\bot$ is a formula, if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so is the implication $\varphi \to \psi$, and if $\varphi$ is a formula and $i$ is an agent then $K_i \varphi$ (read "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$") is a formula.
nodes.title: Epistemic formulas

nodes.summary: Given a type of worlds $W$, a type of atoms and a type of agents, an epistemic model consists of a binary accessibility relation $R_i$ on $W$ for each agent $i$ and a valuation assigning to each world the atoms true there; the world type $W$ is required to be nonempty.
nodes.title: Epistemic models

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At every world of that model the formula $K_1(K_0 p \lor K_0 \neg p)$ holds: agent $1$ knows that agent $0$ either knows $p$ or knows $\neg p$.
nodes.title: Agent 1 knows that agent 0 knows whether the coin is heads

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. The formula $K_1 p$ is false at the heads world: agent $1$ considers the tails world possible.
nodes.title: Agent 1 does not know that the coin is heads

nodes.summary: The epistemic model whose worlds are the two booleans, with $\mathrm{true}$ read as heads and $\mathrm{false}$ as tails, with a single atom $p$ true exactly at the heads world, and with two agents $0$ and $1$: agent $0$ sees the coin, so its accessibility relation is equality of worlds, and agent $1$ does not, so its accessibility relation relates every pair of worlds.
nodes.title: The two-agent coin model

nodes.summary: In every epistemic model, the formula $\bot$ is not valid: it fails at some world.
nodes.title: Falsity is not valid in an epistemic model

nodes.summary: The negation $\neg\varphi$ of an epistemic formula $\varphi$ is the implication $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation of epistemic formulas

nodes.summary: The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of epistemic formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the implication $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of epistemic formulas

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At a world $v$ of that model, the formula $K_0 p$ holds if and only if $v$ is the heads world: agent $0$ sees the coin.
nodes.title: Agent 0 knows the coin is heads exactly at heads

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At a world $v$ of that model, the formula $K_0 \neg p$ holds if and only if $v$ is the tails world.
nodes.title: Agent 0 knows the coin is tails exactly at tails

nodes.summary: In an epistemic model $M$, the disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of two formulas, defined as $\neg \varphi \to \psi$, is satisfied at a world $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ or $\psi$ is satisfied at $w$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a disjunction

nodes.summary: Satisfaction of an epistemic formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined by recursion on the formula, writing $R_i$ for the accessibility relation of agent $i$ in $M$ and $K_i \varphi$ for the formula "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$": an atom $a$ holds at $w$ when the valuation of $M$ makes $a$ true at $w$; $\bot$ holds at no world; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ when $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does;…
nodes.title: Satisfaction in an epistemic model

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". For every epistemic model $M$, every agent $i$ and all formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the formula $K_i (\varphi \to \psi) \to (K_i \varphi \to K_i \psi)$ is valid in $M$: knowledge distributes over implication.
nodes.title: Distribution axiom K

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is euclidean: for all worlds $a$, $b$, $c$, if $a \mathrel{R_i} b$ and $a \mathrel{R_i} c$ then $b \mathrel{R_i} c$. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\neg K_i \varphi \to K_i \neg K_i \varphi$ is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Negative introspection axiom 5

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is transitive. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $K_i \varphi \to K_i K_i \varphi$ is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Positive introspection axiom 4

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is reflexive. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $K_i \varphi \to \varphi$ is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Truth axiom T

nodes.summary: A formula $\varphi$ is valid in an epistemic model $M$ when $\varphi$ is satisfied at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Validity in an epistemic model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
